videos.title: Rarer Than Gold | Every Precious Metal Explained | Everyday Explained
tags: most valuable metals in the world
videos.description:
What makes a metal “precious”? And why are some of them worth more than gold?

In this video, we break down every major precious metal — from well-known ones like gold and silver to lesser-known metals like palladium, rhodium, osmium, iridium, and more. Each metal has its own unique properties, uses, and surprising facts that make it valuable in different ways.

You’ll discover how these metals are used in jewelry, electronics, cars, aerospace, and modern technology, and why some of them are rarer than you might expect.

This video covers:

- Gold, silver, platinum, and other common precious metals
- Rare metals like palladium, rhodium, osmium, iridium, ruthenium, and more
- Real-world uses of each metal
- Interesting facts you probably didn’t know

videos.title: How Do Engineers Build These Bridges? | Every Type of Bridge Explained
videos.description:
How can a bridge weighing thousands of tons stay suspended above a river, valley, or highway? And why does one bridge use massive cables while another relies on arches, steel trusses, or concrete beams?

Bridges are some of the most impressive structures ever built, but every design solves a different engineering problem. In this video, we break down 10 major types of bridges and explain how each one carries weight, distributes forces, and spans the obstacles beneath it.

From the simple beam bridge found on everyday roads to enormous suspension and cable-stayed bridges, you'll discover why engineers choose one design over another and what makes each type unique.

You'll learn how arches handle compression, how trusses distribute loads, how cantilever bridges extend across difficult terrain, why suspension bridges can cross enormous gaps, and how movable bridges allow ships to pass through busy waterways.

We'll also look at the aqueduct bridge, one of history's most remarkable engineering achievements, designed to carry water instead of road or rail traffic.

Whether you're interested in civil engineering, architecture, construction, infrastructure, or simply curious about how bridges work, this video explores the science and engineering behind some of the world's most important structures.

From ancient stone bridges to modern megastructures, these designs have changed how humans cross rivers, valleys, seas, and cities.

videos.title: Where Does Your Recycling Go? | Every Recycled Material Explained | Everyday Explained
videos.description:
What actually happens to the things we throw into recycling bins?

From paper and plastic to metals, batteries, textiles, tires, and electronic waste, different materials require completely different recycling processes. Some can be melted and turned into new products, while others have to be shredded, separated, chemically processed, or broken down into their basic components.

In this video, we explore the major materials that can be recovered and recycled, explaining How each one is processed, what it can become, and what makes recycling it difficult or valuable.


You'll discover how an old aluminium can can become a new product, how worn-out tires can be transformed into useful materials, how food waste can produce compost or renewable energy, and how valuable metals can be recovered from discarded electronics and batteries.

Recycling isn't the same for everything. Understanding what happens to these materials after they're discarded reveals just how much of our everyday waste can actually be turned into something useful again.
